A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VTool-R1. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original chart/table evaluation results in Table 1, training dynamics in Figures 3–4, and tool-use and reward-design observations.

after.justification: V4 retains original experiments and reports additional comparator results in Table 2 and Section 4.5, plus failure examples in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same visual editing tools, at most one tool-use round, GRPO, and outcome-based rewards. V4 clarifies that only the final response is optimized; v1 already explicitly excludes direct optimization of the intermediate tool-invoking response. The full appendix prompt is unchanged apart from formatting.

E1.justification: Both evaluate VWTQ, VWTQ_syn, VTabFact, and horizontal/vertical bar questions from ChartQA. Chart Split and Table Split rename the retained coverage. The new failure examples remain within chart reasoning; the introductory six-finger example is motivation, not an additional reported evaluation.

E2.justification: V4 adds evaluated RL-trained competitors: R1-VL at 2B and 7B in Table 2, and Deepeyes in Section 4.5. This substantially broadens comparison beyond the original untrained Qwen configurations and GPT-4o. GPT-4o remains evaluated, with its results relocated to Table 2.

E3.justification: The added Table 2 comparison introduces a 2B evaluation configuration through R1-VL, alongside 3B/7B VTool-R1 and 7B R1-VL. Retained VTool-R1 model scales, sample counts, split ratios, and decoding settings remain as reported. Newly specified global batch sizes and GRPO parameters document settings without establishing changes to existing runs.

E4.justification: V4 adds four qualitative failure cases covering incorrect reasoning after successful editing, obstructed chart values, incorrect answers without tools, and failed code execution. These supplement the existing success example, training-dynamics analysis, and reward-design observations, without adding a systematic ablation or robustness study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V4's newly disclosed GRPO group size of five concerns sampled training responses, not independent experimental replications.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises 7B chart/table accuracy from 73.1/60.2 to 80.7/71.7 and 32B table accuracy from 79.3 to 84.5. The 7B results now exceed the unchanged direct-inference baselines on both splits. V4 also adds R1-VL results and reports Deepeyes at 60.0 versus VTool-R1 at 80.7, although that comparison's protocol is sparsely specified.

T1.justification: The rollout definition, reward-regularized objective, GRPO objective, and advantage normalization remain mathematically unchanged. V4 adds no theorem, proof, or substantive derivation; its final-response optimization wording clarifies the existing formulation.

C1.justification: The central claim that outcome-based RL teaches interleaved visual and textual reasoning is retained. V4 modestly qualifies priority in the concluding discussion, changing the first framework to one of the first frameworks, and adds an explicit code-release claim.

C2.justification: V4 adds discussion of language shortcuts, failure mechanisms involving visual edits and subsequent reasoning, and an attribution of the Deepeyes performance gap to tools, training, and task design. It also explains multi-image capability as a constraint on future multi-turn extensions. The existing task-scope and single-round limitations remain.

D1.justification: V4 supplies a code repository link and newly reports global batch sizes of 32/256 for tables/charts, rollout group size five, KL coefficient 0.01, and GPU memory capacities. V1's micro-batch size of two is omitted. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish corresponding training changes or verify repository contents.

R1.justification: V4 explicitly positions VTool-R1 alongside Deepeyes and OpenThink-IMG as concurrent frameworks that also learn visual reasoning through tools, substantially expanding discussion of close alternatives. It additionally cites Cache-of-Thought and internal-feedback research while removing several general architecture and preference-optimization references.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work discussion are substantially rewritten, dataset descriptions are consolidated into Table Split and Chart Split, and contributions are reordered and completed. The standalone limitations section is merged into the conclusion, producing substantial narrative revision beyond local copyediting.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a single-column conference layout, restructures the comparisons into two tables, redraws Figure 2, and restyles and reorders Figure 3's panels. Four illustrated failure boxes are added across the main text and appendix. The pipeline and appendix 32B training figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 improves empirical context and transparency through relevant RL-trained comparisons, explicit failure cases, clearer objective wording, and additional training and code-access information. These are useful but limited gains: the revised headline accuracies are unexplained, comparator settings remain sparsely documented, and uncertainty reporting is still absent. Higher reported scores alone do not establish stronger paper quality.
